edges.title: Vaughan Williams dedicates his Fifth to Sibelius
edges.claim: The score of Vaughan Williams’s Fifth Symphony, first performed at the Royal Albert Hall on 24 June 1943, is headed “Dedicated without permission to Jean Sibelius”. Sibelius replied from Finland in June 1946: “I have seldom heard anything that is more English.”

edges.title: Vaughan Williams sets Shakespeare’s moonlit scene for sixteen voices

works.from: The Merchant of Venice, Act V

edges.claim: For Henry Wood’s jubilee concert at the Royal Albert Hall on 5 October 1938, Vaughan Williams took the moonlit scene between Lorenzo and Jessica from Act V of The Merchant of Venice and wrote it for sixteen solo singers and orchestra.

edges.title: Vaughan Williams conducts the Bach Choir and Dorking Passions

works.to: Vaughan Williams’s conducting at the Bach Choir and Leith Hill Musical Festival

edges.claim: Vaughan Williams was musical director of the Bach Choir from 1921 to 1928. In Dorking he rehearsed the St Matthew Passion in the town’s halls, and the Leith Hill Musical Festival choirs sang Bach’s Passions under him.

edges.title: Vaughan Williams edits Purcell’s Royal Welcome Songs
edges.claim: Vaughan Williams edited two volumes of the Purcell Society Edition for Novello: Volume 15 in 1905 and Volume 18 in 1910. Both hold Purcell’s royal welcome songs, and both were later superseded by Bruce Wood’s editions.
